subject: ventures/mosquito-control-program-pricing-calculator
professional: an owner-operator of a multi-truck mosquito/pest barrier-spray franchise who prices seasonal programs (with a licensed pesticide applicator and a small-business CPA checking costing and margin definitions); first check: loaded cost per visit, whether margin and prepay maths hold, and whether chemical cost scales with real dilution/label rates

evidence.correctness: Ran `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the dir: 30 pass, 0 fail. Recomputed independently in Python from the default inputs (formulas re-derived from the README, not copied from calc.mjs): product 15x1.6=24.00, labour 39/60x28=18.20, truck 14/60x11=2.567, direct with 6% re-treat 47.45; visit profit at $95 = 95-47.45-14.25=33.30 (35.05% margin); min price 47.45/0.45... precisely 47.45/(1-0.55)=105.45; min list with 8% prepay 47.45/(0.45x0.92)=114.62; season paid 524.40, profit 161.02 (30.7%); expected seasons (1-0.72^8)/0.28=3.313, lifetime 533.55; capacity 11x4x24/6=176 customers, break-even ceil(6500/161.02)=41. All matched analyze()/toCsv() output of node to the cent. Minor: payback is expressed in weeks of the season, not elapsed weeks.
evidence.completeness: README/page claims checked: per-visit cost breakdown (works), min price per visit and per prepaid season (works), price ladder (in analyze, rendered in index.html), customer lifetime value (works), truck capacity and break-even customers (works), sensitivity table (works), CSV download (toCsv matches). Served index.html over a local http server and loaded it in headless Chrome: module imports resolve, no errors seen; I did not click Run, so the rendered result table was verified only through analyze() and page.test.mjs. No TODO/stub found. VENTURE.yaml stage is prototype, and says the hypothesis is untested.
evidence.verification: 30 tests across calc, page and usage (flat-cost fixtures with hand-checkable numbers, round-trip margin checks, Infinity guard, corrupt-storage). Seeded mutation: in minVisitPrice changed `+ wantPct` to `- wantPct` in the denominator; result 27 pass, 3 fail (tests 4, 5, 6 failed), reverted with git checkout, tree clean. Weaker: no test pins the default-case numbers (105.45/114.62/161.02), route payback has little coverage, and no test exercises the DOM render of the results.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs, calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, index.html script, usage.mjs. Pure functions, closed-form renewal sum (comment says a loop froze the tab), Infinity guard, input sanitising in analyze(). Defects: analyze() silently falls back to DEFAULTS for any non-finite typed value (blank field becomes the example number with no warning, index.html opts() does the same), so a user who clears 'Product cost' gets a price built on a placeholder; only some fields are validated for negatives (visitPrice, yardSqft, seasonsCap, stopsPerDay, startupCost are not); season() and route() recompute season(o, price) up to three times; unrounded money in CSV string via toFixed is fine. canonical is the relative './index.html'.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer text present in README and page (No warranty, not legal/tax/accounting advice), privacy claim backed by page.test.mjs (no fetch/XHR, local imports only). Usage-counting claim backed by usage.mjs. Gaps: llms.txt links to https://duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo/mosquito-control-program-pricing-calculator/ (the old Pages host, which CLAUDE.md says now only redirects) while README/VENTURE.yaml use marisstella.app; README says 'Tests: node --test' (the repo's own guidance is that bare form is rejected by Node 22); the FAQ line 'list price has to be about 8% higher' is approximately right (1/0.92 = 8.7%) but is generic. Page says 'Nothing uploaded' which is true. No unbacked numeric market claim found.
evidence.fitness: Walked a new operator's job: enter yard size, product cost, times, labour/truck rates, get a floor price per visit and per season. Works and the warnings (price below want margin, impossible margin) are useful. Gaps the operator hits quickly: labour is charged on drive minutes once per stop but only the truck's drive minutes count for mileage, one-way semantic is unclear; no per-property variation (a quote is for one yard, no tiered yard sizes); product cost is a flat $/1,000 sq ft with no dilution rate/oz per gallon or label-rate helper; no sales/acquisition cost in lifetime value and no discounting; no sales tax; capacity ignores weather days and that customers are not spread evenly across the season.
evidence.domain: Compared against how barrier-spray franchises and the NPMA/pest-control costing practice price: cost-plus on labour+product+vehicle plus overhead, target gross margin, prepaid season discounts, retention-driven LTV. The method is the standard cost-plus form and margin-on-price is correct (not markup). Departures: overhead and card fees applied as one percent of revenue is fine, but there is no fixed-overhead allocation per route hour, no productivity benchmark (stops per day is typed, not derived from on-site + drive minutes: the defaults imply 11x39 min = 7.2 h so it is consistent, but nothing checks it), no applicator licence/insurance per-hour treatment beyond the user's loaded rate, LTV undiscounted and with no acquisition cost, and no guidance on typical product cost ranges. A senior operator would find it a good first-pass quoting sheet but not a replacement for a route-density model.

defects.what: A blank or non-numeric input silently falls back to the example default (analyze() and opts()), so the output can price the job on a placeholder with no warning.
stopsPerDay is typed independently of onSiteMin and driveMin and never cross-checked against a working day, so the capacity and break-even figures can be unrealistic without any warning.
llms.txt points at the retired GitHub Pages host instead of marisstella.app.
Customer lifetime value is undiscounted and carries no acquisition cost; no test pins default-case outputs.

verdict: The arithmetic is right: seven outputs recomputed in Python from the README's formulas match the code to the cent, 30 tests pass, and a seeded sign flip in minVisitPrice was caught by 3 tests. The weakness is that it is a prototype-level quoting sheet: blank inputs silently take placeholder values, capacity is not cross-checked, product cost has no dilution or label-rate logic, and llms.txt links to a retired host. It is finished against its own README, and it meets the correctness/verification bar, but claims, fitness and domain land at 2, so it is not expert-grade for a working operator.
